headline: A rough week for AI spenders: the Nasdaq had its worst day since June on Friday and its worst month since March 2025, while energy, defense and power gear rose; Brazil had its worst week since 2020, and next week brings the midterms, a Brazil rate decision and a possible US strike on Iran.
summary: The dashboard is still on Oct 29 closes (prices_as_of 2026-10-29, refresh running), so every close below is the Oct 30 close from Massive. On Friday the S&P 500 fell 1.82% to 7,580.07 and the Nasdaq Composite 2.86% to 25,437.00; the S&P ended the week down 0.6% and the Nasdaq 100 lost about 6.5% in October (Barchart via Yahoo). Intel fell 28.6% to 65.76, its worst day since the 1970s, and Amazon 1.4% to 240.35, while Exxon closed at 187.25 and Chevron at 235.52, both above their 2R targets on a close (Massive, CNBC). Brazil's Ibovespa lost 18.12% for the week, its worst since March 2020, and EWZ fell 23.78% (Rio Times, Massive). The scorecard shows 6 swing wins of 10, but it grades on intraday highs; by her rule (a close over the pivot on 1.5 times volume), none of the six swings checked is a finished win. Next week: Apple Monday, the midterms and Brazil's rate meeting Tuesday, Brazil's decision Wednesday, the Bank of England Thursday and the jobs report Friday, with a report that the US warned Gulf allies of possible Iran strikes from Nov 4.

regime.why: Friday was a broad sell: Nasdaq decliners beat advancers about 3 to 1 and the VIX rose 12.9% to 19.42 (Reuters, Yahoo). Money left the AI spenders and chips and went to energy, defense and power equipment, but the S&P 500 is now down three weeks in a row and futures price a 73% chance of a Fed hike in December (Barchart). Oil up 13.6% in October and a possible Iran strike after the vote keep the risk high.

signals.title: Week in review: the market sold the AI spenders and bought what they pay for
signals.since_yesterday: Friday's close: Intel fell 28.6% and the Nasdaq 2.86%, its worst day since June 5, capping its worst month since March 2025.
signals.what_happened: Over Oct 26 to 30, Alphabet fell 12.61% to 279.84, Meta 4.30% to 614.99, Amazon 3.08% to 240.35 and Microsoft 0.50% to 521.91 (Massive, Oct 23 to Oct 30 closes). On Friday Intel fell 28.6% to 65.76 after guiding Q4 to $15 billion to $16 billion and flagging an explosion at its Israel plant worth about $600 million of revenue over two quarters; Amazon recovered from a 6% early drop to close down 1.4% (Barchart via Yahoo, CNBC). Microsoft fell 1.55% on 35.7 million shares, 1.66 times its 50 day average (Massive). The same week the companies that get paid rose: Vertiv's Q3 sales grew 61% to about $4.3 billion with organic orders up more than 100%, and it raised guidance (company release, Oct 28); VRT rose 19.65% for the week despite a 5.46% drop Friday to 232.50. Defense rose too: LHX +9.31%, GD +6.65%, LMT +5.42% (Massive).
signals.so_what: Buyers will still pay for AI demand when the cash shows up in someone's orders, but not for the spending itself. Second order: as long as the spenders keep spending (Amazon plans more in 2027), suppliers like Vertiv keep winning; the risk flips only if a spender cuts its budget. Third order: higher borrowing to fund the build keeps long rates high, which caps what buyers pay for every growth stock. Correction on Intel: Morningstar wrote 31%; Massive's close of 65.76 against 92.07 is a 28.6% drop, and that is the number to use.
signals.for_you: Swing: no AI swing; MT Swing Setup dropped MSFT on Friday, so the scanner now agrees the setup is broken. Long term: MSFT (521.91) is now inside its 423.43 to 527.46 buy zone, but two heavy volume down days (1.86 and 1.66 times average) are distribution; wait for the refresh to confirm 'Buy zone now' and a calm day, then a small first tranche at most. GOOGL and AMZN stay Wait. INTC is far under its old zone; no buy and no put on a 28.6% drop. VRT (232.50) is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' and closed just under its 235.93 zone floor: the up/down volume check fails; watch only.

signals.title: Oil: Brent finished October up 13.6%; a report says the US warned Gulf allies of strikes on Iran as early as Nov 4, while talks move to Doha
signals.since_yesterday: Two opposite reports on Saturday: possible US strikes from Nov 4, and a US delegation said to be joining direct talks with Iran in Doha.
signals.what_happened: Brent's December contract expired Friday at $117.64, up 2.4%, and January settled at $113.43, up $2.63; WTI settled at $104.12. Brent rose 13.6% in October (FinanceFeeds). Seven OPEC+ members meet online Sunday and were likely to keep December output unchanged, three sources told Reuters on Oct 27 (via FinanceFeeds). On Saturday the Times of Israel carried a report that the US warned Gulf allies of possible strikes on Iran as early as Nov 4, the day after the midterms, and another that a US delegation would join direct talks with Iran in Doha after a negotiation breakthrough. Iran's army warned any new attack would spread the war wider (Al Jazeera). A drone hit two fishing boats near Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz (Times of Israel, citing AFP).
signals.so_what: The next week has a fork: a strike would likely send Brent back toward or above $118 to $120, and a deal in Doha could take a big part of the war premium out. Both are plausible, so oil can gap either way on Wednesday. Who pays if oil spikes: airlines and consumers. Who gets paid: refiners and producers, which already reached their targets.
signals.for_you: Swing: take the plan on energy; do not add oil names before Wednesday. DAL (80.15) is inside its 74.44 to 82.72 buy zone and 'Buy zone now' on Oct 29 data, but a strike is a real risk to jet fuel costs: no DAL buy or put until after Nov 4. Puts: none on energy.

signals.title: Brazil had its worst week since March 2020; markets now expect a Selic hold on Nov 4
signals.since_yesterday: The week's total: Ibovespa -18.12%, EWZ -23.78%, and Polymarket odds of a hold rose to 78.4%.
signals.what_happened: The Ibovespa fell 18.12% in the week after Lula's re-election, its worst week since March 2020, and the PTAX dollar rate was R$5.4212 on Oct 30 (Rio Times). In New York EWZ fell 23.78% for the week to 32.46, NU 23.4% to 11.61, ITUB 26.3% to 7.13 and BBD 37.3% to 2.55 (Massive). Itau cut its 2027 Brazil growth forecast to 0.5% from 1.2%, raised 2027 inflation to 6.1% from 4.6%, and sees the Selic at 13.75% through 2027. Polymarket gives 78.4% to no change on Nov 4 and 19.0% to a quarter point cut (Rio Times). EBC also sees a hold as the base case.
signals.so_what: The market already priced a lot of bad news; the next move depends on what Copom says about the weak real and on any fiscal plan from the new government. A hold with a hawkish tone keeps funding costs high for Brazilian banks and NU. A credible fiscal signal could start a relief rally, but that has not happened yet.
signals.for_you: No Brazil buys, swings or new puts before the Nov 4 decision. NU (11.61) is 11.4% under its 13.10 'thesis broken' line and Wait. If you sold the EWZ Nov 20 $37 put from an earlier brief, EWZ closed 12.3% below the strike; with no verdict, the rule is no roll.

signals.title: Scorecard: how the calls did
signals.what_happened: The scorecard (graded Oct 31 on Oct 29 data) shows: swings 20 calls, 10 finished, 6 wins, average +0.8R, 7 open; cash secured puts 13 open, none finished yet (the first expiry is Nov 20); long term buys 116 calls, 49 of 110 beat SPY over 5 days, average 2.71 points behind SPY; signals 74 of 130 right after 5 days, average 0.59 points ahead of SPY. These swing numbers are inflated: the scorecard counts a trigger and a win on an intraday high, not on her rule. Her rule checked with Massive daily bars for six swings: XOM, no confirmed entry before the target (scorecard: 2R win); CVX, never confirmed, best day 1.31 times volume (scorecard: 2R win); WST (383.49 setup), confirmed Oct 29 at 416.67 on 3.35 times volume, open at about 1.59R, target 420.19 not reached on a close (scorecard: 2R win on the 438.27 intraday high); EOG, confirmed Oct 16 at 158.01 on 1.77 times volume, open at about 1.70R (scorecard: open); COP, never confirmed, best day 1.26 times (scorecard: open, and it will likely call it a win on the next refresh because the Oct 30 high of 154.28 touched the 154.23 target); MSFT, never confirmed (scorecard: open, about -0.47R on the Oct 30 close).
signals.so_what: Of the six checked, the scorecard shows three wins; her rule shows no finished win, two confirmed trades still open and four setups that never confirmed. Buying at the confirmation close also shrinks the gain: from the confirm day close, EOG is up about 0.75R and WST is about flat (-0.08R). What works: the energy calls were right on direction, and WST is the clean example of the rule, a breakout on 3.35 times volume. What does not: ZBRA lost twice and ANET once (not rechecked under her rule), and long term buys trail SPY over 5 days, which is too short to judge. Samples are small: 10 finished swings and no finished puts prove nothing yet. Another gap: on Oct 30 PWR was dropped as a put idea because its chart shows lower highs (742.73 Jun, 724.80 Aug, 722.21 Oct 6) and lower lows (593.70 Sep, 527.07 Oct 23), a downtrend the dashboard's moving average check missed.
signals.for_you: Two rule changes are waiting on your yes: (1) grade swings on her rule, a close over the pivot on at least 1.5 times the 50 day volume, so the scorecard stops counting wins that never triggered; (2) add a swing structure check (lower highs and lower lows) to the chart check, which would have flagged PWR. Until then, read the scorecard's swing hit rate as an upper bound, not the real number.

signals.title: Health: an FDA panel backed the agency's doubts on a child myopia drop; Lilly hit a record
signals.what_happened: The FDA's ophthalmic advisory committee met Oct 30 on Sydnexis's SYD-101, a low dose atropine drop for childhood myopia. There was no vote; members broadly supported the FDA's concerns about the single Phase III trial and the supporting literature (Pink Sheet, BioWorld). Lilly closed at a record 1,417.54 on Oct 30, up 11.31% for the week after its Q3 beat and raise (Massive, company release); ARK sold 17,626 LLY shares in ARKK the same day (ARK email).
signals.so_what: For myopia control in children, a setback for an atropine drop leaves contact lens options like CooperVision's MiSight as the main FDA approved tool for now, but Sydnexis is private and the effect on COO is small. Lilly's record shows money still pays for GLP-1 cash flow; ARK's sale is one fund trimming a winner, weak evidence.
signals.for_you: No action. LLY is 'Accumulate on pullback', far above its 1,054.91 to 1,229.49 zone. COO (59.55) is Wait. DXCM rose 5.58% for the week to 82.29 and is still 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' (up/down volume check fails).

history.when: April to September 2002, Lula's first election
history.what: The real lost more than a third of its value from April to late September 2002 as markets feared a Lula government (The Guardian, Sep 27, 2002).
history.lesson: An election shock in Brazil can run a long way, and it eased only once the new government proved it would keep fiscal discipline, as Lula promised in his Letter to the Brazilian People. Wait for the policy signal, not the price.

source.title: Brazilian election damages currency (The Guardian, Sep 27, 2002)

history.when: June 1999 to May 2000, Fed hikes into the tech capex boom
history.what: The Fed raised its target from 4.75% to 6.50% while companies spent heavily on internet and telecom gear (Federal Reserve rate history).
history.lesson: Rising rates punished the spenders with weak cash flow first, and the suppliers later, when budgets were cut. This week matched the first step; the suppliers (Vertiv) are fine until a spender cuts.

source.title: Federal Reserve open market operations: historical target rate changes (Federal Reserve)

cycle.differences: In 2002 the fear came before the vote and lasted months; in 2026 the shock came after it, because markets had priced a Bolsonaro win, and the Selic is already 13.75%. In 1999 the spenders were young and unprofitable; today they are the richest companies in the world, but now they borrow to keep pace.

principle.text: Don't confuse what you wish were true with what is true (Principles).
principle.applied: The scorecard says 6 swing wins out of 10. It is tempting to believe it. But by her own rule, none of the six swings checked is a finished win, and four never triggered. The true record is unknown until the grading is fixed, so size swings as if the edge is unproven.
